scopeNotes: The md items are the headed half of fix-ask-door-multi-directory-host: the session sits in ws while another directory (the third one the anchor item activated) is the host's last-initialized one. 'Answerable' is proven by the observer (request in the session's own pending table), the absence of a 404 reply and the call executing only after the terminal's answer.

'/new' in the TUI opens an empty tab; the host creates the session when the first message is sent. The anchor session was created that way by the TUI (no parent session). Its ask watcher could only be attached 3.1 s after Enter, i.e. after the first turn had started: in that turn the transcript shows exactly one execute part (the forge_shell call) and nothing else, and an ask raised in those seconds would have stayed pending until answered, so the watcher would have seen it.

Voided first attempt of the stale item (counted in no item): the driver refuses background text delivery to a classic console window, so the characters of the typed line did not land, and an Enter sent right after it hit the EMPTY input box — nothing was submitted (transcript: user rows with text = 1, the API-delivered instruction). That window (hwnd 31856116, session ses_df08bc5f6ffe2nJI0BYkPEWOCe, opened 21:27:27Z) then served to rehearse key-by-key typing (74 keys read back exactly), was emptied with Backspace and closed at 21:30:25Z; its own ask watcher saw 0 ask. A 'Switched model to GLM-5.4' line seen in that window was first attributed to the stray Enter — wrongly: the clean stale window of the same item printed the same line as well, in both windows between the first capture (idle) and the first submitted turn (cause not established; the model shown before and after is GLM-5.4 in both). From this attempt on every prompt was typed one key at a time and read back before Enter.

Voided first attempt of the anchor item (counted in no item): with the 0.34.1 official sentence ('call the forge shell tool directly. do not call search and do not look anything up first. …') the model spent its single code call on a wrong call shape — its code bound tools.forge_shell to a variable, tried Object.keys on it and called its .shell member (else .forge_shell) with the command 'cd', i.e. it treated tools.forge_shell as a namespace; the code tool returned 'Unknown tool forge_shell.shell. Use search to find available tools.' forge_shell itself was never called, so the attempt is neither evidence for nor against the anchor (logs/tui-postcheck-anchor-a0342x.json; session ses_df07078a1ffeXwFaQRKPBNYGMM). The item was redone on a fresh '/new' session with one added sentence that spells the name in words: 'in code it is tools dot forge underscore shell, called as a function. it is not a namespace holding a nested tool.' The anchor checks read only the redone session (watcher a0343); the voided session's watcher (a0342) saw 0 ask.

Observed, not a defect this release introduces — how a tool name appears to the model in Code Mode: a model that is forbidden to look the name up may guess it. In this gate's voided anchor attempt the model's reply says, in its own words, that the shell tool's name 'inside the forge_shell namespace was not listed in my catalog', and its call went to a nested name (→ 'Unknown tool'); in the 0.34.1 gate the runbook's sentence of that time — it carried no such prohibition — led the model to spend its call on a tool-catalogue lookup (search) instead, and there the catalogue returned the correct path (recorded in the 0.34.1 evidence). The forge_shell behaviour the anchor item measures was correct in both official runs.
